findings.text: The NON_RENDERER_CALLS comment for the render_mechanism_evidence.py:360 entry states the scratch verification as 'the tree reports 81 instead of 80', but at the reviewed head the tree reports 82 current sites and deleting that entry yields 83 (independently measured). The entry is genuinely load-bearing - removing it re-adds the 360 record - but the two numbers in the comment belong to the predecessor revision's count and a reader re-running the cited verification against this head reaches a different figure. Same class as the prior review's finding 1: an in-record claim that does not reconcile with the module it documents.

The painter guard treats a call as wall-guarded whenever the wall slot is present - len(node.args) > WALL_POSITION_INDEX (9+ positional) or keyword.arg == 'wall' - without checking that the value is not None. nova/media/poloidal.py:147 defaults wall=None means 'no mask', so a call passing wall=None positionally (nine positional args, last None) or by keyword is reported as guarded while the scattered raster stays unmasked. Verified by probe at the reviewed head: a scattered-producer raster handed to draw_flux_contours(a,b,c,raster,d,e,f,g,None) and to draw_flux_contours(a,b,c,raster,d,wall=None) is not flagged, while the same call with no wall slot at all is flagged. Latent: no such call exists in the reviewed corpus, so this is a false-negative class, not a present miss.

Independently reproduced by the review at the reviewed head 08869d26d in the reviewed worktree with byte-code writing disabled: 11 passed in 92.03 s EXIT=0 (/tmp/review-gate.log).

justifications.durability: The rule is pinned by a real, falsifiable control: the positional-wall test reddens when the guard line is removed, which I reproduced by mutation, so the guard fires rather than merely passing. The repair also fixes the predecessor's central durability defect: the test file no longer asserts a frozen inventory count, so a repair batch that fixes a call site cannot turn it red, and the corpus reconciliation lives in a committed, always-zero report script. Weaknesses. The scanner is still wired to nothing but its own test file - no conftest, pyproject or CI reference imports it - so only a manual pytest run exercises it. The positional rule and the keyword rule both recognize the presence of the wall slot rather than a non-None mask: wall=None passed positionally or by keyword is treated as guarded although no raster is blanked (finding 2, latent, no such call in the corpus). And the exemption comment embeds a verification count that has already drifted from the head once (finding 1).
justifications.evidence: Every headline was reproduced first-hand at the reviewed head. The gate at 08869d26d in the reviewed worktree: 11 passed in 92.03 s, EXIT=0 (/tmp/review-gate.log). The report script: 82/4/8, EXIT=0 (/tmp/review-report.log). The declared negative control - delete the len(node.args) > WALL_POSITION_INDEX guard - reproduced by mutation: the crafted positional-wall call is flagged (module.py:2) once the guard is gone and none of the other named controls change, matching the node's 1 failed, 10 passed, EXIT=1 signature. The exemption claim was verified by deletion: removing the render_mechanism_evidence.py:360 NON_RENDERER_CALLS entry adds that record, so the entry is load-bearing. The run also fixes the prior review's finding 5: it now records a real baseline_suite and a real after_suite with log paths, where the predecessor declared both empty. Deductions: the exemption comment's stated scratch-verification counts are stale (finding 1), and the report script's docstring cites an inventory report that exists, but the fragment's drift sentence ('six of them those same shifted or newly-added lines') does not map each of the six extras to its predecessor line, so a reader cannot confirm the shift attribution from the record alone.
justifications.fit: Minimal and idiomatic: one stdlib-ast module, one test file and one small report script, no new dependency, no new abstraction layer, no plan/sprint/ticket identifier in names, comments or subject lines. The relative-path change is the natural fix for the prior basename defect, and the report script matches the read-only inventory-report idiom of the predecessor. Deductions: the report script imports the scanner by sys.path insertion into the tests directory, a coupling that would break if the scanner moved, and it sits under docs/figures/... rather than a tooling directory (a placement fixed by the node's granted path, not the author's choice); and the wall-guard heuristic's dependence on the exact parameter index (finding 2) is a coupling to nova/media/poloidal.py's signature that is documented but not asserted anywhere a signature change would trip.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The reviewed run's goal - close the prior review's five follow-ons on the scattered-field wall scanner: relative paths, positional-wall recognition, a documented exemption list, moving corpus reconciliation out of the test file, and substantiating the 'against base' gate - is met and independently reproduced. I ran the committed report script against the reviewed head: 82 current unguarded sites, 4 inventory lines no longer reported (shafranov_combination_discriminator.py:914 and shafranov_pair_receipt.py:293/309/877) and 8 current sites the inventory lacks (the six shifted/newly-added shafranov_* and frozen_current_flux_image_gate.py lines plus the two disclosed repaired-remeasure measure.py:70 painters), EXIT=0 - matching the fragment's figures exactly, and the arithmetic reconciles (78 − 4 + 8 = 82). UnmaskedCall.path is now repository-relative, so the two same-named measure.py files print as distinct records. Deleting the positional-wall guard makes the crafted control fail, so the guard demonstrably fires. Not full marks because the in-code exemption comment carries stale verification figures that no longer match the head (finding 1).
justifications.scope_discipline: The review range 58d361d2c..08869d26d touches exactly four paths - tests/renderer_wall_scan.py, tests/test_renderer_wall_scan.py, docs/figures/figure-and-solver-audit/fsa-renderer-wall-scanner-guard-form/reconcile_wall_scan_sites.py and docs/evidence/fragments/figure-and-solver-audit/fsa-renderer-wall-scanner-guard-form.html - all inside the run's granted write paths. No renderer, product source, plan, shared index or concurrent-node path is touched. All three commits carry a conventional subject and an explanatory body; a scan of the two changed source files finds no banned plan/stage/ticket label, and no commit message carries an AI trailer. The scanner remains read-only (ast parsing and printing only), and the added report script only reads the corpus and prints, returning 0 unconditionally.
